title: Sammenligne noe tenkt med som om — expressing “as if”
goal: Use som om for imagined resemblance, not a condition or an embedded question.

objectives.statement: Use som om for imagined resemblance, not a condition or an embedded question.

spans.value: Mina and Jonas are having coffee before an announcement about a new department manager. Their colleague Erik seems unusually confident.
Har du sett Erik i dag?
Ja. Han går rundt som om han eier hele kontoret.

blocks.translation: Yes. He is walking around as if he owns the whole office.

spans.value: Og han snakker som om han allerede er avdelingsleder.

blocks.translation: And he talks as if he is already the department manager.

spans.value: Vet du om han har fått jobben?

blocks.translation: Do you know whether he has got the job?

spans.value: Nei. Hvis han får den, får vi sikkert vite det i ettermiddag.

blocks.translation: No. If he gets it, we will probably find out this afternoon.

spans.value: Akkurat nå oppfører han seg bare som om alt er avgjort.

blocks.translation: Right now, he is simply behaving as if everything has been decided.

spans.value: Mina and Jonas do not know whether Erik has got the job. They are comparing his behaviour with an imagined situation: the situation in which he owns the office, is already the manager, or everything has been decided. Norwegian uses

sections.title: Describing an impression with som om

spans.value: . It introduces an imagined situation that resembles what you can see, hear, or experience.

no.value: Erik går rundt som om han eier kontoret.

en.value: Erik walks around as if he owns the office.

spans.value: This does not directly claim that Erik owns the office. It describes the impression created by his behaviour.

no.value: Hun snakker som om hun kjenner alle her.

en.value: She speaks as if she knows everyone here.

no.value: De feirer som om de har vunnet finalen.

en.value: They are celebrating as if they have won the final.

no.value: Du ser ut som om du ikke har sovet.

en.value: You look as if you have not slept.

spans.value: In each case, the first part describes something observable. The clause after
gives the imagined situation that it resembles.

statement.value: when one action, appearance, sound, or situation creates the impression of another situation.

spans.value: The comparison does not have to be completely impossible or false. The speaker may simply be unwilling or unable to state it as fact.

no.value: Det høres ut som om noen banker på døra.

en.value: It sounds as if someone is knocking on the door.

spans.value: Perhaps someone really is knocking. The speaker is reporting how it sounds, not yet presenting the cause as certain.

no.value: Det ser ut som om bussen er forsinket.

en.value: It looks as if the bus is delayed.

spans.value: The bus may indeed be delayed, but the sentence presents this as a conclusion based on appearances.

sections.title: Using som om with a familiar clause pattern

spans.value: ), so continue using the familiar subordinate-clause word order required before this lesson.
As a brief reminder, compare a main clause with a clause after

no.value: Han vet ikke svaret.

en.value: He does not know the answer.

no.value: Han snakker som om han ikke vet svaret.

en.value: He speaks as if he does not know the answer.

spans.value: Recall that familiar subordinate-clause order places

no.value: som om han ikke vet

en.value: as if he does not know

spans.value: The following examples reuse that familiar prerequisite pattern with other sentence adverbs:

no.value: Hun smiler som om hun aldri blir sliten.

en.value: She smiles as if she never gets tired.

no.value: Han oppfører seg som om han alltid har bodd her.

en.value: He behaves as if he has always lived here.

no.value: De ser på meg som om de kanskje kjenner meg igjen.

en.value: They look at me as if they might recognize me.

spans.value: together. It functions as the link between the observed situation and the imagined comparison.

no.value: Katten ligger i sofaen som om den er et menneske.

en.value: The cat is lying on the sofa as if it were a person.

no.value: Nora forklarer reglene som om alle allerede forstår dem.

en.value: Nora explains the rules as if everyone already understands them.

sections.title: Som om is not the same as om

spans.value: can appear in several different meanings. This lesson contrasts
for embedded yes-or-no questions, and normally

no.value: Erik snakker som om han har fått jobben.

en.value: Erik talks as if he has got the job.

spans.value: His way of speaking resembles the behaviour of someone who has got the job.

no.value: Mina spør om Erik har fått jobben.

en.value: Mina asks whether Erik has got the job.

spans.value: introduces a yes-or-no question inside a larger sentence. Mina wants information. There is no comparison.

no.value: Jeg vet ikke om butikken er åpen.

en.value: I do not know whether the shop is open.

no.value: Kan du sjekke om døra er låst?

en.value: Can you check whether the door is locked?

spans.value: These sentences concern uncertainty about a question: Is the shop open? Is the door locked?

no.value: Hun spør om han er syk.

en.value: She asks whether he is ill.

no.value: Han ser ut som om han er syk.

en.value: He looks as if he is ill.

spans.value: The first sentence reports a question. The second describes an appearance.

sections.title: Som om is not a condition

spans.value: A condition states the circumstance under which another event, result, or possibility applies. Norwegian normally uses

no.value: Hvis Erik får jobben, blir han avdelingsleder.

en.value: If Erik gets the job, he will become the department manager.

spans.value: Getting the job is the condition for becoming manager.

no.value: Erik oppfører seg som om han allerede er avdelingsleder.

en.value: Erik behaves as if he is already the department manager.

spans.value: This sentence does not set a condition. It compares Erik’s present behaviour with an imagined situation.

no.value: Hvis det regner, tar vi bussen.

en.value: If it rains, we will take the bus.

no.value: Det høres ut som om det regner.

en.value: It sounds as if it is raining.

spans.value: The first sentence tells us what will happen on a condition. The second reports an impression based on sound.

no.value: Hvis Sara kjenner sjefen, kan hun spørre ham.

en.value: If Sara knows the manager, she can ask him.

no.value: Sara snakker som om hun kjenner sjefen godt.

en.value: Sara talks as if she knows the manager well.

spans.value: In the conditional sentence, Sara’s knowledge affects what she can do. In the comparison, her manner of speaking creates an impression.

no.value: Han snakker om han vet alt.

en.value: Intended meaning: He speaks as if he knows everything.

spans.value: For imagined resemblance, use the complete expression

no.value: Han snakker som om han vet alt.

en.value: He speaks as if he knows everything.

spans.value: alone does not express the intended comparison.

no.value: Hun ser på meg hvis hun ikke kjenner meg.

en.value: 'Not: She looks at me if she does not know me. (for the intended meaning)'

spans.value: This describes a condition: she looks at me in circumstances where she does not know me. It does not mean that her look creates a particular impression.

no.value: Hun ser på meg som om hun ikke kjenner meg.

en.value: She looks at me as if she does not know me.

spans.value: Treating the comparison as a confirmed fact

no.value: De har vunnet kampen.

en.value: They have won the match.

no.value: De jubler som om de har vunnet kampen.

en.value: They are cheering as if they have won the match.

spans.value: The first sentence presents the victory as fact. The second describes the impression created by their cheering. They may have won, but the sentence itself does not confirm that.
Brief reminder inside the complete construction

no.value: Hun snakker som om hun vet ikke hva som skjedde.

en.value: Intended meaning: She speaks as if she does not know what happened.

no.value: Hun snakker som om hun ikke vet hva som skjedde.

en.value: She speaks as if she does not know what happened.

spans.value: The familiar prerequisite pattern used here is:

no.value: som om hun ikke vet

en.value: as if she does not know

no.value: Barnet løper rundt som om det har masse energi.

en.value: The child is running around as if it has loads of energy.

no.value: Tobias gir ordre som om han bestemmer her.

en.value: Tobias gives orders as if he is in charge here.

no.value: De hvisker som om møtet allerede har begynt.

en.value: They are whispering as if the meeting has already started.

spans.value: It is also common after expressions describing an appearance, sound, or feeling.

no.value: Det ser ut som om alle har gått hjem.

en.value: It looks as if everyone has gone home.

no.value: Det høres ut som om naboene har fest.

en.value: It sounds as if the neighbours are having a party.

no.value: Det føles som om vinteren aldri tar slutt.

en.value: It feels as if winter never ends.

spans.value: The same construction can express a speaker’s critical or humorous attitude.

no.value: Han klager som om dette er verdens største problem.

en.value: He complains as if this were the biggest problem in the world.

no.value: Du pakker som om vi skal være borte i en måned.

en.value: You are packing as if we are going to be away for a month.

no.value: Hun beskytter den gamle koppen som om den er svært verdifull.

en.value: She protects the old cup as if it were extremely valuable.

spans.value: The tone comes from the comparison and the context.
itself does not automatically mean that the speaker is mocking someone.
Later that afternoon, Mina and Jonas receive the announcement.
Nå vet vi om Erik fikk jobben.

blocks.translation: Now we know whether Erik got the job.

spans.value: Ja, og det gjorde han ikke.
Likevel smiler han som om ingenting har skjedd.

blocks.translation: Even so, he is smiling as if nothing has happened.

spans.value: Kanskje han bare prøver å virke rolig.

blocks.translation: Perhaps he is only trying to appear calm.

spans.value: The new information changes what Mina and Jonas know, but it does not change the function of
. Mina observes Erik’s smile and compares it with the behaviour of someone unaffected by the announcement.
Notice the contrast between information and impression:

no.value: Nå vet vi om Erik fikk jobben.

en.value: Now we know whether Erik got the job.

no.value: Erik smiler som om ingenting har skjedd.

en.value: Erik smiles as if nothing has happened.

spans.value: The first sentence concerns the answer to a question. The second interprets observable behaviour through an imagined comparison.

Imagine a new scene at a railway station. The departure board has stopped updating. One traveller repeatedly checks the time, another is unpacking food for a long wait, and a railway employee continues working calmly. The travellers do not yet know whether the train has been cancelled.

prompt.value: Read the two office comments. Choose the interpretation that identifies the observable behaviour and imagined situation in both comments. Mina: «Erik smiler som om ingenting har skjedd.» Jonas: «Erik ser ut som om han ikke er bekymret.»

options.text: Mina vet at ingenting har skjedd, og Jonas vet at Erik ikke er bekymret.
options.why: It turns both imagined situations into facts and removes the comparison meaning.

options.text: Mina spør om ingenting har skjedd, og Jonas beskriver hva som skjer hvis Erik ikke er bekymret.
options.why: It replaces imagined resemblance with an embedded question and a condition.

options.text: Mina og Jonas legger merke til Erik, men de trekker ingen sammenligning med en forestilt situasjon.
options.why: It mentions observation but supplies no imagined situation for either comment.

options.text: Mina kan observere at Erik smiler som om ingenting har skjedd; dette er en forestilt sammenligning, ikke et faktum. Jonas kan observere at Erik ser ut som om han ikke er bekymret; også dette er en forestilt sammenligning, ikke et faktum.
options.why: It identifies both observable behaviours and both imagined situations, and it treats neither imagined situation as established fact.

stem.value: Which interpretation correctly explains both comments?

explanation.value: Som om introduces an apparent or imagined comparison, rather than a factual reason, condition, or question.

payload.feedback: Replace hvis with som om. This changes the intended conditional connector to the taught imagined-comparison connector.

prompt.value: Combine the three observation–imagined-situation pairs into one natural Norwegian sentence. Use som om for each pair: he laughs and everything is fine; he looks as if nothing has happened; and he sounds as if he is calm.

After Erik’s result, answer in Norwegian. Explain the difference between om in å vite om noe skjedde and som om in å smile som om ingenting har skjedd. Then write one additional sentence about Erik’s behaviour using som om for an imagined comparison.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the response explains the two connector meanings and includes one additional natural Norwegian sentence with som om. Accept natural wording variants that preserve the distinction and imagined meaning; do not require exact wording.

criteria.instruction: Explains in Norwegian that om introduces whether something happened, while som om presents an imagined comparison.
Writes one additional natural Norwegian sentence about Erik’s behaviour using som om to connect an observable behaviour with an imagined situation.

prompt.value: Write 3–4 short Norwegian sentences about this station scene: the departure board has stopped updating; one traveller repeatedly checks the time; another unpacks food for a long wait; and a railway employee continues working calmly. The travellers do not know whether the train has been cancelled. Use som om in a comparison for each visible behaviour. Use these familiar imagined-clause ideas: toget er forsinket, det blir lenge å vente, and ingenting har skjedd.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the response includes all three observations and uses som om to connect each visible behaviour with an imagined situation. Accept natural Norwegian variants that preserve the three requested meanings and the target construction; do not require exact wording.

prompt.value: Answer in Norwegian. State when Norwegian uses som om. Write one sentence about behaviour or appearance using som om. Briefly explain why your sentence expresses a comparison with an imagined situation, not a condition with hvis or an embedded yes-or-no question with om.
